hint: New trigger entries: nothing records in between; a tap on the Quick Settings tile, the home screen widget, the shortcut or the floating microphone, or a press of a volume key or of a Bluetooth headset's voice key, opens the same dictation sheet as the digital assistant

New permissions: display over other apps (only for the floating microphone, off by default), start at boot (only to bring back a floating microphone that is on after a restart), a special use foreground service (only keeps the floating microphone on screen, never records) and nearby devices (Android 12 and later, asked only when the headset voice key opens the sheet, to take the headset's voice recognition and microphone over). The key trigger is turned on in the system accessibility settings and only filters keys
feature: Quick Settings tile (Voice command): add it in the Triggers group of the settings (Android 13 and later confirm through the system; older versions show the manual steps) and tap it in Quick Settings to speak; on the lock screen you can dictate right away and unlock only before sending or copying (ColorOS and HyperOS ask for the unlock first); a long press of the tile opens the Triggers settings

Floating microphone: off by default and asks for the permission to display over other apps when turned on; a round button you drag along the screen edge and tap to speak; the button records nothing itself, stays on screen with a quiet notification (which can turn it off) and comes back after a restart while it is on; it hides while the dictation sheet shows and can show together with the floating ball of 3-Stove Agent

Home screen widget (Tap to speak) and the shortcut of a long press on the app icon (Voice command) both open the dictation sheet; the settings can put the widget on the home screen and show the manual steps where the launcher cannot

Key trigger: an accessibility service that only filters keys and never reads the screen content, turned on in the system accessibility settings; by default a hold of volume down for about 0.8 seconds opens the dictation sheet, and it can be a hold of volume up or a double press of volume down instead; a short press still changes the volume, and keys are left alone while the screen is off or during a call

Bluetooth headset voice key: a long press on the headset's voice key or touch area opens the dictation sheet (3-Macaw Speech answers the voice command request VOICE_COMMAND). With Nearby devices allowed it listens through the headset's microphone and every press works. When another app answers too, the system first asks which app to use. Turn it off with Headset voice key in the Triggers group of the settings

Every entry opens the same sheet as a long press of the power button: through the assistant session while 3-Macaw Speech is the default digital assistant, otherwise the same sheet directly; when the system does not show the assistant session (for example after a tile tapped on the lock screen asks for the unlock), the sheet opens directly as well
Packaged applications can use speech recognition and model management through a separate entry; microphone access follows each application's own permission
fix: The dictation sheet records as soon as it opens: while the model still loads (the first time, or after 5 idle minutes) the first words are no longer lost, and a short phrase such as hello no longer goes unanswered

hint: First release. The speech module in scripts needs AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} ({{ required_host_version_code }}) or later; the plugin screens, system TTS engine, system voice input, speech recognition service and digital assistant do not depend on AutoJs6

Recognition and synthesis models are not part of the package and are downloaded from the plugin screens or a script; the app as a whole is conveyed under the GNU GPL 3.0 or later (the speech runtime statically links eSpeak NG), and every release comes with the corresponding source
feature: Speech plugin of AutoJs6: once enabled in the Plugin Center, scripts use speech recognition, wake words, voice activity detection, speech synthesis and model management through the speech module
Built-in sherpa-onnx {{ sherpa_onnx_version }} speech runtime and silero VAD v5 voice activity detection model, with one package per ABI for 4 ABIs

Model management: downloads the offline speech models of the signed model catalog from the AutoJs6 shared assets releases, falling back to the official sherpa-onnx releases; every file is checked by SHA-256 before use, with resumable downloads, local import (tar, tar.bz2, zip), removal and default models; models limited to non-commercial use or without a declared license need their license accepted first

Speech recognition of WAV files (8, 16, 24 or 32-bit integer or float, any sample rate and channel count, resampled to 16 kHz mono in the plugin) with timed segments, plus language, emotion and event tags for SenseVoice models; streaming models accept hotwords

Dictation sessions on the microphone or on fed 16 kHz PCM report ready, partial and final results, endpoints, voice activity and the end; the silence that ends a sentence, the no-speech timeout and the longest duration are adjustable; streaming models update partial results word by word, offline models segment by segment
Voice activity detection lists the speech segments of a WAV file with the bundled silero VAD

Wake words: open-vocabulary keyword spotting; Chinese keywords are spelled in the pinyin of their customary reading, English words in the phones of the model's lexicon, and model tokens may be written directly; a hit can start a dictation round on the same recording

During a microphone session the plugin keeps recording with a microphone foreground service and its notification, so a session started while AutoJs6 is in the foreground goes on after AutoJs6 moves to the background or the screen turns off; one microphone session runs at a time; without the microphone permission sessions fail with PERMISSION_DENIED and name the permission screen

Speech synthesis: the installed synthesis models (VITS, Matcha and Kokoro; the catalog has 5 Chinese and English models) turn up to 8000 characters of text into a WAV file sentence by sentence, at the model's sample rate; a speaker and a speed (0.5 to 2 times) can be chosen, progress counts the characters done, and the synthesis can be cancelled at any time; a model with a single speaker ignores a chosen speaker and says so

System TTS engine: once a synthesis model is installed, 3-Macaw Speech can be chosen in the text-to-speech settings of the system, and AutoJs6's tts module and other apps read aloud with it; every speaker is one voice, bilingual models add an English voice for every speaker, and the speech rate follows the system or app setting; without an installed model the engine reports missing voice data
Home screen: shows the speech runtime version, the number of installed models, the microphone permission (with a button to grant it) and whether 3-Macaw Speech is the preferred system TTS engine

Models on the home screen, grouped into recognition, wake words, synthesis and voice activity detection, with size, languages and license: download, pause, resume, cancel, delete and set as default; download progress also shows in a notification; models limited to non-commercial use or without a declared license ask you to accept their license first, and a download on mobile data or another metered network asks before it starts

Import a local model from a tar, tar.bz2 or zip archive or from a folder: files that match a catalog model are registered as that model, other files become your own model after you fill in its kind, model type, name, languages and ID

Try it out: live dictation (partial results in gray) with a choice of model and language, a wake word trial that lists the hits with their keyword and score, and speech synthesis of your text with a choice of model, speaker and speed, played back or saved as a WAV file; leaving the screen releases the microphone

System voice input: microphone buttons in other apps, such as 3-Stove Agent, can use the offline recognition of 3-Macaw Speech: say one sentence in a bottom sheet and the recognized text goes straight back to that app; it ends after a pause, or stop or cancel it earlier; it follows the endpoint sensitivity and voice activity detection of the settings and can be turned off in their recognition group

Digital assistant: after choosing 3-Macaw Speech as the default digital assistant app in the system settings, long press the power or Home button (or use the assist gesture) and say one sentence in a bottom sheet; the recognized text can be edited, then a button hands it to an app that takes voice commands, such as 3-Stove Agent or 3-Stone AI, or you copy it or speak again; nothing is sent before you tap a button. It also works on the lock screen and unlocks before sending or copying. It never reads the screen and does not listen in the background. The recognition group of the settings shows whether it is the default assistant and opens the system settings to choose it

System speech recognition service: apps that use the Android speech recognizer (SpeechRecognizer) can name 3-Macaw Speech directly and get its offline recognition, with partial results; once it is the default recognition service, apps that name none use it too. On Android 11 and lower, choosing it as the digital assistant usually makes it the default as well; from Android 12 on, choose it separately in the system's voice input setting (some phones lack this setting). When another app keeps a wake word listening through 3-Macaw Speech (3-Stone AI, for one), the digital assistant, the system voice input, the speech recognition service and the tryout screen still get the microphone: wake word detection pauses meanwhile and resumes by itself afterwards

Settings: language, night mode, theme color and launcher icon (following AutoJs6 by default); the default recognition and synthesis models, endpoint sensitivity, voice activity detection, speaker, speed and a default voice per language for the tryout screen and the system TTS engine (scripts keep the documented defaults); when idle models are released, catalog refresh and cleanup of leftover files; the settings button of 3-Macaw Speech in the system text-to-speech settings opens this screen

About: version, the release history included with the plugin, update checks (automatically at most every 12 hours, a release can be ignored) and the licenses and notices: the app as a whole is conveyed under the GNU GPL 3.0 or later without any warranty, with the third-party notices, the full GPL text, the Unicode Terms of Use and where the corresponding source is
Launcher icon: adaptive icon (light), adaptive icon (dark), adaptive icon (automatic, the default) or transparent background icon
Screens, README, Plugin Center instructions and changelog in 10 languages: Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong, Taiwan), English, French, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Russian and Arabic
